text:
The Senators and Sharks meet again nine days after San Jose beat Ottawa 6-2, a game our numbers say the Sharks deserved to win only 28% of the time (the share of simulated replays they take). Ottawa lost 6-5 in overtime at LAK on Wednesday and is without Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele. San Jose came back from two goals down to beat VAN 3-2, and is missing Alexander Wennberg and Igor Chernyshov. Collin Graf has stepped into both spots, now skating beside Celebrini and Smith.

On chance creation, Ottawa has taken 50% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, while San Jose sits at 44% and gives up 4.00 expected goals per 60. The Sharks' results have run ahead of their chances, with goaltending doing the lifting. Projected starter Alex Nedeljkovic is +4.6 goals saved above expected this season, while Ottawa's projected Samuel Ersson is -3.2 and was -17.8 last year. Ottawa's power play (0.80 expected goals a game) faces a penalty kill that allows 0.90, and the Senators take five penalties a game.

Watch Tim Stützle, who had three assists against LAK and is 37% to score, and Macklin Celebrini, 43% to score and 82% for a point. Mason Marchment is one goal from 100 career goals. Our under-the-radar picks: Ottawa's Stephen Halliday, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous, and San Jose's Ivar Stenberg, 55% for a point with his ice time up.
